meta.title: Nephrology Literature Update
meta.query: Clinical nephrology — RCTs, systematic reviews & meta-analyses (humans, English)
meta.source: Generated by Google NotebookLM, grounded in PubMed (NLM) abstracts. Each entry links to its PubMed record and DOI.
meta.note: Summaries and PICO are NotebookLM analyses of the source abstracts; criteria marked “not specified” were not stated.

articles.authors: Alam T, Saad M, Ibrahim T, Rajdeep D, Jamshaid Z et al.
articles.title: Effect of fourth-line antihypertensive therapy on clinic systolic blood pressure in resistant hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: This meta-analysis of 11 RCTs involving 3,931 adults found that aldosterone-targeted therapies provide significant SBP reductions in resistant hypertension. The largest reductions were seen with lorundrostat (MD -11.70 mmHg [95% CI -16.07, -7.33]) and baxdrostat 2 mg (MD -10.10 [-12.63, -7.58]), while spironolactone also showed efficacy (MD -7.95 [-10.10, -5.80]).

pico.population: Adults with resistant hypertension (uncontrolled BP despite ≥3 medications)
pico.intervention: Fourth-line antihypertensive agents (e.g., lorundrostat, baxdrostat, spironolactone, aprocitentan)
pico.outcome: Reduction in clinic systolic blood pressure (SBP)

appraisal.bottom_line: Aldosterone-synthase inhibitors (lorundrostat, baxdrostat) and spironolactone significantly lower clinic SBP by approximately 8-12 mmHg in resistant hypertension.
appraisal.relevance: Provides evidence-based guidance for selecting the most effective fourth-line agent when standard triple therapy fails.
appraisal.caveat: A planned network meta-analysis was not possible due to statistical inconsistency, and long-term cardiovascular outcomes were not assessed.

articles.authors: Tsioufis K, Kyriakoulis KG, Vakka A, Stamataki N, Tatakis F et al.
articles.title: Single Interventions (Pharmacological or Renal Denervation) Are Not Sufficient to Achieve Blood Pressure Control in Resistant Hypertension: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 58 studies (n=4,579) showed that a single add-on intervention (RDN or drug) reduces 24-hour systolic ambulatory BP by -11.3 mmHg (95% CI, -12.3 to -10.2). However, only 35% (95% CI, 28-42) of patients achieved blood pressure control targets during follow-up.

pico.intervention: Addition of a single pharmacological or device-based (renal denervation) intervention
pico.outcome: 24-hour ambulatory systolic BP reduction and hypertension control rate

inclusion: Studies assessing antihypertensive effects of adding a single intervention in true resistant hypertension

appraisal.bottom_line: Single add-on interventions like RDN or fourth-line meds reduce SBP by ~11 mmHg, but two-thirds of patients still fail to achieve BP control.
appraisal.relevance: Highlights that most resistant hypertension patients require integrated combination strategies rather than a single 'silver bullet' intervention.
appraisal.caveat: The analysis was primarily conducted using a single-arm framework, and there was no significant difference found between RDN and pharmacotherapy.

articles.authors: McIlroy DR, Wallace SK, Forbes A, Peyton P, Story DA et al.
articles.title: Perioperative intravenous fluid and chronic kidney disease: long-term follow-up of the Restrictive versus Liberal Fluid Therapy in Major Abdominal Surgery (RELIEF) randomised trial.
articles.summary: Long-term follow-up (90 days to 48 months) of 1,670 RELIEF trial participants found no difference in the risk of new or progressive CKD between restrictive (56%) and liberal (53.4%) fluid regimens (adjusted OR 1.13 [95% CI 0.91-1.41]). There were also no differences in lowest recorded eGFR or maximal eGFR change from baseline.
inclusion: Follow-up data between 90 days and 48 months after surgery

appraisal.bottom_line: A restrictive perioperative fluid regimen does not significantly increase the risk of developing or worsening CKD compared to a liberal regimen (aOR 1.13).
appraisal.relevance: Provides reassurance that the transient increased risk of AKI seen with restrictive fluids may not lead to long-term renal decline.
appraisal.caveat: The findings are based on a post hoc analysis and limited by approximately 50% loss to follow-up from the original trial.

articles.authors: K Rajan A, Ioana Onofrei M, Rudra A, Paul S, Shanbhag V et al.
articles.title: Clinical pharmacokinetics of colistimethate sodium and formed colistin in patients with renal impairment or on dialysis modalities: a systematic review and implications for precision dosing.
articles.summary: This review of 13 studies (n=450) found that standardized colistin dosing often fails to reach pharmacodynamic targets (fAUC/MIC ≥12) in patients with renal impairment. Dialysis parameters are major determinants of clearance, with extracorporeal removal accounting for up to 67% of total drug clearance in SLEDD.

pico.population: Adults with renal impairment or receiving renal replacement therapy (RRT)
pico.intervention: Intravenous colistimethate sodium (CMS), formed colistin, or colistin sulfate
pico.outcome: Pharmacokinetic parameters and achievement of pharmacodynamic targets

inclusion: Studies reporting PK of IV CMS or formed colistin in adults with renal impairment or on RRT

appraisal.bottom_line: Standard colistin dosing is frequently inadequate in renal failure; individualized dosing integrating renal function and RRT modality is essential to ensure efficacy.
appraisal.relevance: Critical for nephrologists and intensivists managing multi-drug resistant infections in patients with fluctuating renal function or on dialysis.
appraisal.caveat: Pharmacokinetics showed high variability across small cohorts, and the review included only 450 total patients across 13 studies.

articles.authors: Huang S, Luo J, Yu G, Zhu Y et al.
articles.title: Efficacy and safety of BCMA-directed bispecific antibodies in relapsed and/or refractory systemic AL amyloidosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: Analysis of 8 cohorts (80 patients) treated with BCMA-directed bispecifics showed a pooled hematologic overall response rate of 91% (95% CI: 87%-93%). Significant renal response was achieved in 34% (95% CI: 14%-62%) of these relapsed/refractory patients.

pico.population: Patients with relapsed and/or refractory (R/R) systemic AL amyloidosis
pico.outcome: Hematologic overall response rate (ORR) and organ (cardiac/renal) response

inclusion: Studies involving teclistamab or elranatamab for R/R AL amyloidosis

appraisal.bottom_line: BCMA-directed bispecific antibodies produce deep hematologic responses (91%) and meaningful renal recovery (34%) in refractory AL amyloidosis.
appraisal.relevance: Identifies a highly effective rescue therapy for patients who have failed daratumumab and other standard plasma-cell directed treatments.
appraisal.caveat: A high rate of severe (Grade ≥3) infections (25%) necessitates aggressive antimicrobial prophylaxis and monitoring.

articles.authors: Martinez-Martinez MU, Tejada-Llacsa PJ, Prokop LJ, Crowson CS, Murad MH et al.
articles.title: Efficacy and safety of belimumab and anifrolumab in systemic lupus erythematosus: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A network meta-analysis of 11 RCTs (n=8,607) found that both anifrolumab (OR 1.78 [95% CI 1.41-2.24]) and belimumab (OR 1.62 [95% CI 1.38-1.90]) improved SRI-4 response vs placebo. While anifrolumab was superior to belimumab for BICLA response (OR 1.56 [95% CI 1.10-2.21]), renal-specific outcomes did not differ significantly between treatments.

pico.population: Adult patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)
pico.intervention: Belimumab or anifrolumab plus standard of care
pico.outcome: Disease activity responses (SRI-4, BICLA, BILAG organ-domains)

inclusion: RCTs comparing belimumab or anifrolumab plus SoC vs placebo plus SoC in adult SLE

appraisal.bottom_line: Anifrolumab and belimumab show similar SRI-4 efficacy in SLE, though anifrolumab may be more effective for BICLA response at the cost of higher herpes zoster risk.
appraisal.relevance: Assists clinicians in choosing biologics for SLE patients, emphasizing the need to balance clinical benefit with the high risk of viral infections (OR 4.74 for shingles with anifrolumab).
appraisal.caveat: The superior BICLA response for anifrolumab over belimumab is based on indirect evidence and should be interpreted with caution.

articles.authors: Yuan Y, Lei S, Duan A, Li J et al.
articles.title: Effects on mortality of different blood purification techniques in sepsis patients: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
articles.summary: This umbrella review of 42 meta-analyses found that while mortality generally favored blood purification over conventional care, effect sizes were inconsistent and certainty of evidence was low. Polymyxin B hemoperfusion showed a relatively consistent trend toward lower mortality compared to RRT-based strategies.

pico.intervention: Extracorporeal blood purification (e.g., polymyxin B hemoperfusion, RRT-based strategies)

inclusion: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses evaluating mortality across extracorporeal blood purification modalities in sepsis

appraisal.bottom_line: Blood purification in sepsis may offer survival benefits, particularly with polymyxin B hemoperfusion, but current evidence is too low-quality to be definitive.
appraisal.relevance: Encourages a cautious, phenotype-informed approach to using blood purification in the ICU rather than routine implementation.
appraisal.caveat: Most included reviews were of low or critically low methodological quality due to risk of bias and inconsistency.

articles.authors: Backston K, Buehrer B, Ezgü D, Sivaram P, Tanna S et al.
articles.title: Novel biomarkers for acute kidney injury in high-risk pediatric populations: a systematic review.
articles.summary: A systematic review of 53 studies identifies NGAL, KIM-1, and cystatin-C as the most promising indicators for early AKI detection in children. Other markers like the product of TIMP-2 and IGFBP-7 and interleukin-18 also show potential as early predictive indicators of injury.

pico.intervention: Novel AKI biomarkers (e.g., NGAL, KIM-1, Cystatin-C, TIMP-2 x IGFBP7)
pico.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy (AUC, sensitivity, specificity) for early AKI detection/prediction

inclusion: Assessing diagnostic biomarkers for AKI in high-risk pediatric populations

appraisal.bottom_line: NGAL, KIM-1, and Cystatin-C are reliable early indicators of pediatric AKI that outperform traditional creatinine-based diagnosis.
appraisal.relevance: Supports the clinical integration of novel biomarkers into risk-stratification tools for earlier AKI intervention in children.
appraisal.caveat: Widespread clinical implementation still requires further validation across diverse high-risk pediatric cohorts.
